NEW NOTE
# Cooperative promotion and the cost of mixed matching corners

19 October 2026. Research note; the submitted manuscript is unchanged.
This continues the exact ledgers in ATTACHMENT_CORRECTED_COLLAR_COMPENSATION.md
and the geometry in DIAGONAL_WITNESS_CHAINS.md. The results below are written
general proofs, with independent finite controls. They do not establish the
unrestricted grid inequality or a new universal coefficient in the 5/6 bound.

## 1. Objective-preserving promotions on any finite graph

A feasible pair consists of a vertex set T and a matching M disjoint from T,
such that every vertex of T has at most one neighbor in the occupied set
A=T union V(M). Its objective is |T|+|M|. Write deg_A for occupied degree.

**Bundle lemma.** Choose distinct edges x_i y_i of M and orient each by
choosing its endpoint x_i. Set X={x_i}, Y={y_i}, and remove these edges
from M while adding X to T. The new occupied set is exactly A minus Y.
The resulting pair is feasible if and only if

    deg_(A minus Y)(x_i)<=1 for every i.                 (1)

The objective is unchanged, T grows by the number of chosen edges and M
shrinks by the same number.

Proof. Matching disjointness makes X,Y,T pairwise disjoint and ensures
the surviving edges avoid T union X. Existing selected vertices only lose
occupied neighbors. Thus the only new feasibility conditions are precisely
(1). Each removed matching edge contributes exactly one new selected vertex.
This proves both directions and the objective assertion. QED.

In particular, an endpoint of occupied degree at most two can always be
promoted alone: its mate is removed, leaving degree at most one. This has
no neutrality, attachment, tile or boundary hypothesis. Repeating single
promotions stops with every remaining matching endpoint of degree at least
three. Unlike the restricted neutral move, this general move need not
preserve any tile charge, marked cap, residual component or certificate.
Those objects must be reconstructed after normalization.

**Cycle lemma.** In a bipartite graph, fix one side. Orient each matching
edge from its endpoint x on that side to its mate y. Retain as candidates
the edges with deg_A(x)=3. Put a directed arc i to j, for distinct candidate
edges, when x_i is adjacent to y_j. Every directed cycle of distinct
candidate edges can be promoted simultaneously.

Proof. For each edge of the directed cycle, the removed set Y contains
both its own mate and the next edge's mate. These are distinct occupied
neighbors of x_i. Its initial occupied degree is three, so its remaining
degree is at most one. Apply the bundle lemma. QED.

In physical grid edges this is an M-alternating even cycle. A two-vertex
directed cycle is a square with two opposite matching edges. This cycle
is different from either a tile-adjacency cycle or a shared-blank double
link; none of their resource counts may be substituted for another.

**Normalization theorem.** Every finite feasible pair in a bipartite graph
has an objective-preserving representative, retaining all original T,
such that all matching endpoints have occupied degree at least three
and both degree-three dependency digraphs are acyclic.

Proof. Repeat an eligible single promotion, or, if none exists, a directed
cycle promotion on either side. Each move strictly decreases the number
of matching edges and preserves feasibility and objective. There are at
most the original |M| moves. On termination neither type is available,
which is exactly the asserted condition. QED.

Consequently an objective maximizer chosen to maximize |T| already has
this stronger condition. A terminal point for single moves alone need
not have it. No confluence or order independence is asserted. Recomputing
degrees and running a linear directed-cycle search after each move gives
O(|M| (|V|+|E|)) time and O(|V|+|E|) storage. On a bounded-degree grid this
is quadratic time. The supplied checker independently validates every
resulting feasible pair, rather than relying on a cycle-search assertion.

## 2. A two-sided chain bound with an explicit transition penalty

Use TL,TR,BL,BR corner order. Suppose the saturated tiles

    S_i=(r0+i,c0-i), 0<=i<v, v>=2,

all have selected corners TR,BL and exactly one matching endpoint at TL
or BR. Call this choice their P-state. Include both intervening tiles
(r0+i,c0-i-1) and (r0+i+1,c0-i) for every consecutive pair, and assume
all those tiles are deficient. Let R consist of exactly these 3v-2 tiles.
Assume every matching endpoint in the full configuration has occupied
degree at least three. Let a count P-state changes along the chain.

**Local gap lemma.** If consecutive owners have the same P-state, each
of their two intervening tiles has b-t>=1.

Proof. Place the two owners east and south of the northwest intervening
tile Q. Their selected corners force Q.BR blank. First let both owners
have P at BR, hence their TL corners blank. The external right neighbor
of Q.TR and external lower neighbor of Q.BL are therefore blank.

Every deficient tile has b>=t. If Q had b=t, its forced blank would
imply t=b=1, with its other two vertices P. T at TL would then have
two occupied internal neighbors, impossible. T at TR would leave BL
as P with just one occupied internal neighbor, an external blank below,
and at most one occupied external neighbor to the left. That P would
have degree at most two, also impossible. T at BL is symmetric. Thus
b-t>=1. This argument only uses actual occupied degrees, even if a mate
crosses the region boundary.

The southeast intervening tile has TL forced blank, with its TR and BL
external neighbors both P. Again b=t would mean t=b=1. T at BR has two
internal occupied neighbors. T at TR or BL has an occupied internal
neighbor and its external P neighbor. All cases are impossible. Rotate
the complete picture by 180 degrees for the common TL P-state. QED.

The intervening tile sets of distinct consecutive pairs are disjoint:
the first kind has coordinate sum r0+c0-1 and the second r0+c0+1,
and their row coordinates identify the link uniquely. Thus the v-1-a
equal-state links contribute without overlap:

    D>=2(v-1-a).                                        (2)

Let sigma count matching edges with a deficient endpoint in R and a
saturated endpoint outside R, and eta the reverse crossings. There are
v saturated matching endpoints in R, so k=v-eta. The exact original
configuration ledger 2rho(R)=-D+k+sigma gives

    2rho(R)<=2-v+2a+sigma-eta.                          (3)

For a homogeneous chain this is rho(R)<=1-v/2+(sigma-eta)/2.
For instance, v>=4 and sigma<=eta supply at least one unit of negative
charge, enough for tile-disjoint sources with total original charge at
most one. If disjoint cores of this kind cover every positive source and
the remainder has nonpositive charge, the usual additive ledger proves
coefficient one for that class. Tile disjointness, the source allowance
and the boundary imbalance are essential hypotheses, not conclusions
of the normalization theorem. No resource is reused: (2) sums actual
disjoint deficient tiles, and each source/core enters the regional sum once.

## 3. A complete single-promotion-terminal mixed diamond

Here is an 8 by 4 grid configuration, with zero-based vertex coordinates:

    T={(0,0),(0,2),(2,3),(3,0),(3,2),
       (4,1),(4,3),(5,0),(7,1),(7,3)}
    M={ (2,2)--(2,1), (2,0)--(1,0), (1,1)--(1,2),
        (5,1)--(5,2), (5,3)--(6,3), (6,1)--(6,2) }.

All remaining vertices are blank. The following vertex array also lists
all labels, with each two by two block a tile:

    T B | T B
    P P | P B
    ----+----
    P P | P T
    T B | T B
    ----+----
    B T | B T
    T P | P P
    ----+----
    B P | P P
    B T | B T

Each T has exactly one occupied neighbor. The two saturated-owner P
vertices (2,2),(5,1) have occupied degree four; the other ten P vertices
have degree three. This is a full feasible pair with no eligible single
promotion. Its objective is 10+6=16, exactly half of the 32 vertices.

Take R={(1,0),(1,1),(2,0),(2,1)} in tile coordinates. Its owners are
(1,1) with P at TL and (2,0) with P at BR. Both intervening tiles have
t=b=1. Thus

    D=0, k=Q=2, sigma=eta=0, j=2, rho(R)=1.

There is no free blank after the one-blank-per-T reservation. Its witness
graph consists of two isolated owners. The exterior has charge -1;
the full grid has charge zero. Therefore occupied degree at least three
alone does not imply nonpositive regional charge, even with no saturated
boundary transfer. This is a counterexample to that regional rule, not
to the global grid inequality. For (3), v=2,a=1 attains 2rho(R)=2, so
the coefficient two on a cannot be reduced while keeping the other terms
fixed under these hypotheses.

## 4. Arbitrarily large connected receivers, and their exact repair

Stack r copies of this 8 by 4 block, shifting each by (8i,0). At a block
boundary, occupied vertices in the two facing rows have opposite column
parities; hence no new occupied adjacency is created. The resulting
8r by 4 pair remains feasible and terminal for single promotions, with
|T|=10r, |M|=6r and objective 16r, exactly half the grid size.

Include the four central tiles of every block and, between consecutive
blocks, add tile (4i+3,1) and tile (4i+4,1). This tile-connected receiver
R_r has 6r-2 tiles. It is not claimed residual-connected. Each first
bridge tile has t=1,b=1 and charge zero; each second bridge tile has
t=1,b=2 and charge -1/2. Its P is matched inside the two-tile bridge.
Thus the bridge pairs introduce no saturated attachments. Directly,

    D=r-1, k=Q=2r, sigma=eta=0,
    j=2r+(r-1)=3r-1, rho(R_r)=(r+1)/2.

The added crossing in each bridge pair is the edge from the second
bridge tile's P to the omitted tile in column zero. Each second bridge
has one free blank, adjacent to exactly one neighboring owner. Hence H
has 2r isolated owners, p=r-1 private blanks, d=u=0. The exact witness
ledger is again 2rho=2r-(r-1)=r+1. The remainder has charge -(r+1)/2.
So single-promotion-terminal pairs have unbounded positive charge on
tile-connected receivers. This still does not obstruct a representative
maximizing |T|, since the following cooperative repair increases |T|.

In the top half of each block, simultaneously promote (2,1),(1,2) and
remove (2,2),(1,1), deleting their two matching edges. Each promoted
vertex initially has degree three and loses both these removed neighbors.
This is exactly a two-cycle in the dependency digraph. Now (1,0) can
be promoted singly, removing (2,0). In the bottom half, simultaneously
promote (5,2),(6,1) and remove (5,1),(6,2); then promote (6,3), removing
(5,3). These are the 180-degree reflected moves.

All moves occur strictly inside a block, so perform them independently
in every block. The final pair has no matching edges and 16r selected
vertices, retains the original 10r selected vertices, and preserves the
objective. This proves for every r that the displayed obstacle is
eliminated by the stronger normalization. It does not prove that every
mixed-state receiver in that normal form is compensated.

## 5. Reproduction and remaining question

Run:

    python3 develop/check_cooperative_promotion.py --output output/cooperative-promotion-check.json

The checker independently reconstructs every matching, occupied degree,
selected-neighbor constraint, regional charge and blank allocation. It
checks r=1 through 32 and all eight grid symmetries, all 12,752 feasible
pairs on the 2 by 2, 2 by 4 and 2 by 6 controls, and all 81 local ternary
tile states for each implication in the local gap lemma. Each algorithmic
move is rechecked by actual coordinates. These finite checks support the
proofs above; they are not substitutes for the all-size arguments.

The scoped Lean module SubQuorum/MixedPChainCompensation.lean proves both
finite gap implications by kernel reduction and the conditional transition
charge bound by integer arithmetic. The bridge from actual occupied degrees
to the local predicates, the disjoint-link geometry, the graph normalization
theorem and the all-r family remain written proofs. The combined audit now
contains 22 declarations; it does not claim full formalization of this note.
External review and priority for this new note are pending.

The next precise question is whether acyclicity of both degree-three
dependency digraphs forces enough private/exterior compensation at
mixed P-state transitions, or whether a further physical obstruction
survives. Degree-four endpoints and interactions between selected-corner
orientations remain outside the homogeneous run bound. General grid
equality and a universal improvement of 5/6 remain open.


EXACT LEDGER BACKGROUND
# Removing ordinary pressure faces: the exact internal-attachment debt

19 October 2026. This strengthens the pressured-collar sufficient theorem by
removing the pressure requirement on every unmarked tile. Receiver regions
may be thick, contain degree-four tiles or be disconnected. The replacement
is an explicit internal saturated-attachment budget, and a corrected parity
term. The unrestricted grid problem remains open.

## Definitions

Use the same feasible pair (T,M), aligned 2x2 tiles and full-configuration
charges as in `PRESSURED_COLLAR_COMPENSATION.md`. A deficient tile has at
most one T vertex; a saturated tile has exactly two. Write P for matching
endpoints and B for blank vertices. All quantities refer to the original
configuration, including crossings between regions to be combined later.

Let R be any finite tile region. Choose L distinct marked tiles, each with
one BB face and its two perpendicular faces pressured by actual occupied
neighbors. There is no pressure, tree or degree condition on any other tile.
Define:

- D(R): the sum of b_Q-t_Q over deficient tiles Q in R only;
- k(R): matching edges wholly in R joining a deficient tile to a saturated
  tile; within-tile matching edges are not included;
- sigma: matching edges from a deficient tile in R to a saturated tile
  outside R;
- eta: matching edges from a saturated tile in R to a deficient tile
  outside R;
- Q: matching endpoints in saturated tiles of R;
- j: all physical matching edges crossing R's boundary.

The letter Q here is an endpoint count, not a tile name. Every saturated
tile has at most one P vertex, so Q also counts the saturated tiles with P.

## Local facts without pressure

Every deficient tile satisfies b_Q>=t_Q. For t_Q=0 this is immediate. For
t_Q=1, its selected corner has two internal neighbors and at most one may
be occupied, so at least one is blank. No external pressure is needed.

A saturated tile has t_Q-b_Q=p_Q with p_Q<=1. Adjacent selected corners
force both remaining corners blank. For diagonal selected corners, both
remaining corners cannot be occupied, since each T would have two occupied
internal neighbors. The vertex partition then gives b_Q=2-p_Q.

There is no matching edge between two saturated tiles. Both endpoints would
be their tiles' unique P corners, with diagonal T corners. Across the shared
tile face the two companion corners would be adjacent T vertices, each
already adjacent to its own P corner, violating feasibility.

The marked-tile argument from the pressured lemma gives b_Q-t_Q>=2 and
also makes every marked tile deficient. Summing over deficient tiles yields

    D(R) >= 2L.                                         (1)

## Exact ledger and corrected parity

**Theorem.** For every region and marking satisfying the stated hypotheses,

    Q = k+eta,
    2rho(R) = -D(R)+k+sigma,
    D(R) mod2 = (j+Q) mod2,
    2rho(R) <= -2L+k+sigma-((j+Q) mod2).                (2)

Proof. Every saturated P endpoint is matched to a deficient tile. Splitting
its mate according to membership in R proves Q=k+eta; the matching gives
one edge per endpoint and there is no double counting.

For each deficient tile the earlier elementary identity is

    2rho_Q=t_Q-b_Q+s_Q,

where s_Q counts matching edges to saturated tiles anywhere. Its sum over
R has sum s_Q=k+sigma. Saturated tile charges are zero. This proves the
second identity without a missing incoming-boundary correction.

For total counts t,b in R, the saturated local identity gives

    D(R)=b-t+Q.

The exact matching vertex partition 4|R_tiles|=t+b+2mu+j implies b-t and j
have the same parity. Thus D has parity j+Q. Its lower bound (1) is even,
so D>=2L+((j+Q) mod2). Substitute in the exact charge identity. QED.

Equivalently, using the existing regional ledger directly gives
2rho=t-b+sigma-eta=-D+Q+sigma-eta=-D+k+sigma.
Incoming saturated endpoints do not create a free deficit or an extra
resource; their count cancels eta exactly. Internal saturated attachments
remain as actual debt.

For a boundary check, let j_DD count matching crossings whose two tiles
are deficient. Then j=j_DD+sigma+eta, so j+Q has the same parity as
j_DD+sigma+k. Incoming endpoints do not independently create parity slack.

The written proof and explicit all-length constructions received an
independent ACCEPT; see docs/reviews/2026-10-19-attachment-collar-assessment.md.
The later BLANK_WITNESS_COMPENSATION.md supplies a geometric certificate
that can pay nonzero internal attachment debt using distinct free blanks.
That later theorem is outside this accepted review.

## Uniform compensation and the pressure-free sufficient class

For pairwise tile-disjoint source regions U_i, disjoint from R, assume
sum rho(U_i)<=L. Full-configuration additivity and (2) give

    2rho(R union all U_i) <= k+sigma-((j+Q) mod2).        (3)

In particular k+sigma<=((j+Q) mod2) pays all source regions simultaneously.
This includes **k=sigma=0 for arbitrary unpressured or thick receivers**,
with unrestricted eta. No assumption about residual-component closure,
matching directions, capacity-two visits, or the shape of R is used.

The one budget D is summed over disjoint deficient tiles; each marked tile
is used once and each actual internal attachment contributes once to k.
An overlapping second application to the same receiver remains invalid.
Packing disjoint compensated cores with a nonpositive remainder proves
|T|+|M|<=mn/2 on this enlarged sufficient class. The universal 5/6 bound
and arbitrary internal-attachment compensation are not settled by (3).

The previous pressured theorem is recovered exactly: pressure on every
tile implies Q=0 and hence k=eta=0, restoring its parity j mod2.

## Two necessary corrections, with explicit physical witnesses

All coordinates are zero-based in a 10-by-16 rectangle. Vertices not listed
as selected or matching endpoints are blank.

**The parity cannot remain j mod2 after pressure is dropped.** Let

    T={(4,10),(5,11)},
    M={((4,11),(4,12))},
    R=the single tile at tile coordinate (2,5).

Each T has exactly one occupied neighbor, the P at (4,11). R is saturated
with Q=eta=j=1, k=sigma=D=0 and rho=0. The old uncorrected bound at L=0
would assert 2rho<=-1 and is false. The corrected parity j+Q is even and
(2) is exact. This refutes a pressure-free parity rule, not the grid target.

To include a genuine marked terminal, add tile (2,2) to R and matching
edges (4,5)--(5,5), (3,4)--(3,5), (6,4)--(6,5). Its left face is BB and
top/bottom faces are pressured. Then L=1, D=2, rho(R)=-1 and Q=eta=j=1.
The old bound would say 2rho<=-3, still false. Formula (2) gives -2 exactly.
This receiver is disconnected, as permitted by the general theorem.

**The internal debt coefficient cannot be decreased.** Take

    T={(2,2),(3,3),(3,5)},
    M={((2,3),(2,4)),((2,5),(1,5))},
    R=the two adjacent tiles (1,1),(1,2).

All selected vertices have one occupied neighbor. The first tile is
saturated; the second has labels PP/BT and (r,d)=(0,1). Thus
Q=k=j=1, eta=sigma=D=0, 2rho(R)=1. Formula (2) is exact. Dropping k
would assert rho(R)<=0, which fails. This is a connected physical
obstruction to that local rule; its whole-grid objective is only 5<80.

There is an unbounded connected version. For every ell>=1, use a
6-by-(2ell+8) rectangle, keep the preceding T and two matching edges,
and include the two lower tiles and upper tile row0, columns2,...,ell+1
in R. Add the following matching edges:

- (0,4)--(1,4);
- (1,2c)--(1,2c+1) for 3<=c<=ell+1;
- (0,2c+1)--(0,2c+2) for 2<=c<=ell+1.

All endpoints are distinct; every selected vertex keeps its one occupied
neighbor. Every upper tile is full P, with h=1,r=1,d=2 and zero charge.
The residual path goes upward from the deficient gadget and turns right
through the upper row; its final edge leaves R into a deficient tile.
Thus R is an induced tile path, k=Q=j=1, D=eta=sigma=0 and rho(R)=1/2
at every length. Its global objective is 2ell+5<6ell+24=mn/2. This is an
all-length obstruction to paying the internal debt merely by a long or
bent receiving route, not a counterexample to the grid inequality. QED.

## Verification and scope

The general argument above is the proof; finite enumeration is auxiliary.
`develop/check_attachment_collar_compensation.py` checks local unpressured
states and actual matching fixtures, with the original regional ledger and
eight grid symmetries. The thick-region fixtures include a degree-four tile
and an incoming saturated endpoint with no pressured face, outside the
previous theorem's hypotheses.

`formal/SubQuorum/AttachmentCollarCompensation.lean` kernel-checks the local
unpressured implications and conditional corrected parity/aggregate counts.
The geometry-to-count and attachment identities retain the written proof;
end-to-end grid formalization is not claimed. The local combined audit
passes ten declarations (six original, four new), with axiom sets contained
in {propext, Quot.sound}. Finite controls pass 40 unpressured deficient
states, ten saturated states, 45 physical regions and 360 symmetry images,
including debt-path lengths zero through forty. These finite ranges do
not replace the all-length construction or general proof.

```sh
python3 develop/check_attachment_collar_compensation.py --output output/attachment-collar-controls.json
python3 scripts/check_collar_formal.py --lean /path/to/lean4.33.0/bin/lean --output output/attachment-collar-formal-check.json
```

The earlier collar ACCEPT covers its earlier hypotheses, not this new
extension or its two obstruction rules. The same-conversation follow-up
2e81689f-ebdb-4ef9-902c-0c3af27da282 is pending; its original stream and
prompt identity are retained. See `output/attachment-collar-oracle-review.json`.

Haobo Ma and Wenlin Zhang used AI tools for search, double-checking and proofreading.


DIAGONAL AND TILE-CYCLE BACKGROUND
# Shared-blank components are straight diagonal chains

19 October 2026. This refines BLANK_WITNESS_COMPENSATION.md using the
physical geometry of saturated attachment owners. The abstract multigraph
allocation theorem allows arbitrary cycles. The actual grid witness graph
has a substantially smaller class: straight diagonal chains, with at most
two distinct edges per consecutive owner pair. The only possible cycle
resources are parallel pairs.

## 1. The shared-corner displacement lemma

Keep the feasible pair, tile region, marked caps, reserved internal blanks,
free deficient blanks F and saturated attachment owners A of the preceding
note. Tile coordinates are integers; a tile (r,c) has corner coordinates
(2r,2c),(2r,2c+1),(2r+1,2c),(2r+1,2c+1), in TL,TR,BL,BR order.

Let a free blank z have two distinct owners S and S'. Both selected
vertices witnessing ownership are external neighbors of z, outside its
deficient tile. They must be its two external neighbors: one vertical,
one horizontal. Those neighbors lie in diagonally opposite owner tiles.

More explicitly, if S witnesses z through its selected corner x, then
the other owner tile and its selected corner are forced:

| Corner x of S | S'-S | Corner of S' |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TL | (-1,-1) | BR |
| TR | (-1,+1) | BL |
| BL | (+1,-1) | TR |
| BR | (+1,+1) | TL |

For example, if x is S.TL=(2r,2c), z is either (2r-1,2c) or
(2r,2c-1). In the first case z lies at the BL corner of tile (r-1,c),
whose other external neighbor is (2r-1,2c-1). In the second it lies at
the TR corner of tile (r,c-1), with exactly the same other external
neighbor. Thus S'=(r-1,c-1) and its witnessing corner is BR. The other
three rows follow by reflection. Missing outer-boundary neighbors simply
prevent the corresponding shared blank; they create no exception.

For each diagonally adjacent owner pair there are only two possible
physical shared blank vertices, the two common neighbors of their
nearest selected corners. Therefore an edge pair has multiplicity at most
two. Each such vertex belongs to F separately; one may be absent,
reserved, occupied or in a saturated tile, leaving fewer edges.

## 2. Classification theorem

**Theorem.** Each connected component of the shared-blank multigraph H
lies on one straight tile diagonal. All its owners have the same selected
diagonal orientation. After parallel edges are collapsed, it is a finite
path, possibly a single vertex. Along that path every link has multiplicity
one or two.

Proof. An owner is saturated with a matching endpoint, so its selected
corners are either TL/BR or TR/BL. In the first case the displacement
table permits only steps (-1,-1) and (+1,+1); every neighbor has the
same orientation and the invariant c-r is constant. In the second,
only (-1,+1) and (+1,-1) occur, the neighbor orientation is again the
same and c+r is constant.

Induction along any walk proves the assertion for a whole connected
component. For either orientation, there is at most one possible owner
at each row coordinate on its fixed line, and edges join consecutive
rows. A finite connected subset is therefore an interval of these rows;
a missing row or missing link separates components. Its underlying
simple graph is exactly a path. The preceding lemma bounds multiplicity
by two. QED.

In particular, the graph is bipartite by row parity and has no simple
cycle of length at least three. Turning a physical residual path does
not turn a shared-blank component: the two graphs describe different
incidences.

## 3. Exact payment with double links

Let d count unordered owner pairs joined by two distinct free blanks.
If H has v owners and c components, its underlying paths have v-c links,
so e=v-c+d and its cycle rank is exactly mu=d. Write p for private
degree-one free blanks and u for unused degree-zero free blanks as before.
The exact charge identity becomes

    2rho(R)=-2L+sigma+c-d-p-u.                    (1)

A component admits a distinct adjacent blank for every owner exactly
when it has a double link or a private blank. A chain with all links
single and no private blank leaves exactly one owner unmatched.

For a double link, assign its two distinct blanks to its two endpoints
and assign every other chain vertex its edge toward those endpoints.
For a private blank, root the chain at its owner, assign that private
blank to the root and each other vertex its edge toward the root.
These constructions use each actual blank at most once. Conversely,
a chain with v vertices, all links single and no private blank has only
v-1 incident blanks. Omitting one root attains precisely v-1 assignments.

For disjoint source regions of total charge at most L,

    2rho(R union sources)<=sigma+c-d-p-u.         (2)

Thus d+p+u>=c+sigma is a sufficient aggregate compensation condition.
An unpaid single-link chain costs exactly one doubled-charge unit.
Every double link, private blank and unused free blank contributes one
unit to the signed regional ledger; no abstract longer cycle is available.
Several such resources in one component can pay deficits of other
components additively, even though an adjacent assignment cannot cross
between components.

Equation (1) is independent of reservation choices because c-d-p-u=k-|F|.
A different valid reservation can change the incidence and component
description, but cannot manufacture additional aggregate charge slack.
An augmentation that merely changes reservations is therefore not, by
itself, a new numerical compensation theorem.

## 4. Double-link payment consumes a tile cycle

Let G_R be the simple graph of physical tile adjacency induced by R,
with cycle rank nu_R=|E(G_R)|-|R|+components(G_R). Then

    d<=nu_R.                                           (3)

Proof. The two distinct free blanks between a consecutive owner pair
lie in the two different intermediate deficient tiles of their unit
tile square. All four tiles belong to R. Thus each double link gives
a distinct unit-square cycle in G_R. Distinct owner pairs cannot give
the same square: its saturated owner diagonal and deficient intermediate
diagonal are fixed.

These unit-square cycles are linearly independent over the field of
two elements. In any nonempty selection of them, choose a topmost square.
Its upper edge belongs to that square and to no other chosen square,
so their edge symmetric difference is nonempty. To bound their number
by nu_R, choose a spanning forest of G_R. A cycle is determined by its
edges outside that forest: a nonzero difference supported only on a
forest cannot have even degree everywhere. There are exactly nu_R
nonforest edges, proving the dimension bound and (3). QED.

**Forest obstruction.** If G_R is a forest, H has no double links at all:
every shared-blank component is a single-link diagonal chain. Consequently

    2rho(R)=-2L+sigma+c-p-u.                            (4)

Paying worst-case disjoint source charge L by this regional certificate
is possible exactly when p+u>=c+sigma. Mere length, branching or bending
of a tree-shaped tile receiver cannot create a cycle payment resource.
Private or unused free blanks must pay the remaining chain components.
If the actual source charge is s<=L, the exact union charge is instead
(sigma+c-d-p-u)/2-(L-s); unused source allowance may also compensate.
A failed worst-case certificate alone does not imply positive union charge.

The cycle ranks of G_R, the shared-blank graph H and the residual matching
graph are different quantities. Here a tile cycle can support a beneficial
double link. In EXTERIOR_COMPONENT_BUDGETS.md a residual cycle consumes
capacity. The two effects must not be substituted for each other.

## 5. Arbitrarily many independent double-link resources

Use the a-owner staircase of BLANK_WITNESS_COMPENSATION.md, a>=2:

    S_i=(1+i,a-i), 0<=i<a,
    W_i=(2+i,a-i), 0<=i<a-1.

The S tiles have labels BT/TP; W tiles have BP/PP. All original matching
edges are as in that note. For any subset I of {0,...,a-2}, add tiles

    V_i=(1+i,a-i-1), i in I,

with labels PP/PB. Match V_i.TL to V_i.BL and V_i.TR to its immediate
upper external neighbor. In vertex coordinates the new endpoints are

    (2i+2,2a-2i-2)--(2i+3,2a-2i-2),
    (2i+2,2a-2i-1)--(2i+1,2a-2i-1).

All these coordinates lie in the original (2a+4)-by-(2a+6) rectangle.
The first edge family uses even columns and its two stated rows; the
second uses odd columns and different columns for different i.
At each of its rows, the new endpoints lie strictly to the left of
the original occupied vertices in that row. Consequently the new matching edges have disjoint
endpoints and avoid the original endpoints and selected vertices.

The only new occupied vertices adjacent to an S tile lie across its
nonselected corners. The added V_i.BR=(2i+3,2a-2i-1) remains blank and
is adjacent to S_i.BL and S_(i+1).TR. Thus all original T vertices keep
exactly their existing internal P neighbor. Every V_i has t=0,b=1,
h=1,s=0,crossing=1, hence r=1,d=1 and rho=-1/2.

The BR blank is a second shared blank for the pair S_i,S_(i+1);
the original W_i.TL is the first. There are no new owners. Other
original free blanks keep their owners, giving

    c=1, d=|I|, p=u=0, k=a,
    D=a-1+|I|, sigma=eta=0,
    rho(R_I)=(1-|I|)/2.                         (5)

Hence one chain can contain arbitrarily many double-link resources.
One such link pays its own initial shortage; every further double link
supplies another half-unit of negative regional charge. These are
distinct physical blanks, not repeated uses of one cycle certificate.
The full-grid objective is 4a-1+2|I|, still below mn/2.

The original tile-adjacency graph is a path. Every added V_i has exactly
the two neighbors S_i,S_(i+1) in R_I; no two V_i are tile-adjacent.
It adds one vertex and two edges without changing connectivity.
Therefore nu_(R_I)=|I|=d: bound (3) is sharp for arbitrarily large d.
